Subject: Payment checkout failures — 500 spike (12/10 08:40-09:05 PST)

Hi Jasmine,

We saw a sharp spike of 500 responses hitting our checkout flow starting ~08:40 PST this morning and lasting until ~09:05 PST. During the window our telemetry shows ~12% of checkouts returning 500 and some customers reporting retries. This started right after a rolling config update tied to autoscaler tuning.

Impact:
- Region: us-west-2
- Peak failure rate: ~12% for checkout POST /v1/checkout
- Estimated revenue exposure: ~45 minutes of degraded conversions for about 1,200 active sessions

We attached a sample log bundle (clearmarket-500s-window-logs.zip) and a brief timeline. Can you confirm whether Redwood saw any availability gap or preemption event on your side that maps to 08:40–09:05 PST? If eligible under our contract, we will file an SLA claim and would appreciate an initial confirmation and a path to request remedy/credit.

We'd also like to schedule a short post-incident call to review the RCA and mitigation plan. Availability this week: Tue/Thu mornings PST.

Thanks,
Dana Li
Sr. Ops Manager, ClearMarket
support@clearmarket.com

Jasmine / Laura — quick internal update after a first-pass investigation: 

- Infra observed a short preemption cluster in the us-west-2 serving pool coincident with the window. Host-level logs show a surge of container restarts between 08:41:12 and 08:59:07 PST.
- Continuous-batching queues experienced transient backpressure; several requests hit fallback paths that returned 500s for weighted percent of traffic.
- I attached a snapshot of the SLO rolling window (slo-snapshot-20261210.csv) with the availability curve — it crosses our 99.9% window for a ~17-minute interval within the customer's reported timeframe.

Preliminary take: there is a credible match between the customer's observed 500s and our infra preemption/restart window. That suggests the event is within scope for an availability review and potential proportional credit, pending final alignment on exact impact window and contract terms.

Next actions:
- Infra to produce a signed log bundle and trace bundle for 08:30–09:15 PST (expected EOD 12/11).
- Jasmine to confirm cross-check with ClearMarket's logs and agree on the adjudication window.
- Product/Legal to advise on whether the event qualifies for the standard pro-rata remedy or an exception.

Karthik
Head of Production Reliability, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Thank you for your patience. We've completed a preliminary review of the incident and can confirm the following: 

- Confirmed incident window: 08:41:12–08:59:07 PST on 2026-12-10 (us-west-2).
- Root cause (preliminary): autoscaler churn caused a burst of container preemptions; fallback routing introduced transient 500 responses for a subset of traffic.
- Eligibility: Based on our initial assessment and the SLO snapshot, this event crosses the availability threshold for a limited interval and is therefore eligible for our standard proportional remedy calculation. Final eligibility and credit amount will be confirmed after delivery of the full trace bundle and legal signoff.

What we are proposing now:
1) Incident evidence bundle (signed) — infra will provide full traces and host logs by EOD 2026-12-12 (we will send the download link).
2) Provisional remedy: we will begin preparing a pro-rata credit calculation for the affected billing period; once legal has reviewed, we'll issue a formal Credit Memo or apply an account credit (your preference).
3) Postmortem call: Thu 2026-12-14 09:00 AM PST (30 minutes) — agenda: timeline, root cause, mitigations (autoscaler tuning rollback and guardrails), and remediation plan. Please confirm whether this time works and whether you prefer a shared DocuSign agreement or an immediate credit memo.

For transparency I've attached the incident dashboard link and a placeholder DocuSign request for a credit agreement — we will not finalize anything until you confirm.
